message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge a security deposit, but it cannot exceed **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit or **three months’ rent** for a furnished unit.
• The deposit must be held in a **separate, interest‑bearing account** (unless the landlord is a bank).
• Within **30 days** after you move out, the landlord must return the deposit or provide a written itemized list of deductions and the remaining balance. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any receipts for repairs you made.
• Take photos of the unit before you move out. | | **Habitability** | • Texas law requires landlords to keep the premises in a **safe and habitable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity).
• Landlords must repair major problems within a reasonable time after notice. | • Report problems in writing (email or text) and keep a copy.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or pursue a **repair‑and‑deduct** remedy (pay for repairs yourself and deduct from rent, but only if the landlord is in default). | | **Rent Payment & Late Fees** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Landlords may charge a late fee, but it must be **reasonable** (usually no more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if you’re having trouble. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlords must give **reasonable notice** (typically 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies.
• “Reasonable notice” means a notice that is reasonable under the circumstances, not a fixed number of hours. | • Ask for a written notice if you’re unsure. | | **Privacy** | • Landlords cannot harass or threaten tenants.
• They cannot use the premises for any purpose other than what’s allowed by law. | • Keep a record of any harassment. | | **Discrimination** | • Under the **Fair Housing Act** and Texas law, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income. | • If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party can terminate a lease with proper notice: **30 days** for month‑to‑month leases, or the notice period specified in the lease.
• Landlords must provide a written notice of termination. | • Keep a copy of the notice and confirm receipt. | | **Eviction Process** | • Texas requires a **written notice** (usually 3 days for nonpayment of rent, 30 days for lease violations, 60 days for no‑cause termination of month‑to‑month).
• If the landlord files an eviction lawsuit, you have the right to a hearing and to present evidence. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• Attend the court hearing and bring all relevant documents. | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to fix a major problem, you may pay for the repair and deduct the cost from your rent, but only if the landlord is in default and the repair is necessary for habitability. | • Get a written estimate and keep receipts. | | **Right to a Written Lease** | • While Texas does not require a written lease for month‑to‑month rentals, having one protects both parties. | • Request a written lease if you’re moving into a new unit. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify who pays utilities. If the landlord pays, they must maintain the utility service. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • The lease may restrict subletting; if it does, you need the landlord’s written consent. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Maintenance of Records** | • Landlords must keep records of rent payments and maintenance requests. | • Keep copies of all correspondence and receipts. | ### Where to Get Help | Resource | What it offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** | Consumer complaints, landlord‑tenant mediation | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | Discrimination complaints | | **Local tenant‑rights groups** | Legal clinics, workshops | | **Legal Aid of North Texas / Texas Legal Services** | Free or low‑cost legal assistance | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Read the lease thoroughly** – note rent amount, due date, security deposit, pet policy, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 2. **Document the unit’s condition** – take photos and list any existing damage. 3. **Ask for a written lease** – even if you’re signing a month‑to‑month agreement. 4. **Confirm who pays utilities** – and how they’re billed. 5. **Know your rights** – keep this guide handy. Feel free to ask if you need more detail on any specific point or if you’re dealing with a particular issue!
